data.narrative:
Oxa is a Series D autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $103M to date. The broader sector includes 8 private peers (Wayve, Waymo, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro among them) and no public comparables. A narrow peer set of same-stage or adjacent-stage companies proved insufficient for statistical median benchmarking, necessitating reliance on a single methodological approach.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised ($103M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement yields $154M. This reflects the expected increase in company value between institutional funding rounds at this stage. The peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient datapoints within tightly defined cohorts; relying on all-sector medians would introduce material cross-stage and scale bias.

The triangulated valuation range is $131M to $178M, with a midpoint of $154M. This single-method result carries elevated uncertainty relative to multi-method triangulation. Key sensitivities include: (1) the appropriateness of the 1.5x multiplier to Oxa's specific risk and growth profile relative to frontier-tech benchmarks, and (2) the absence of revenue, growth rate, or unit economics data to anchor relative valuation. A fuller appraisal would benefit from either narrower peer identification or direct comparable transaction precedents within autonomous vehicle infrastructure.
